methods.estimand: Change in observed monthly medians within the same original station and analytical cohort.
methods.aggregation: Agreeing repeated results within an activity count once. Different activities in the same calendar month contribute to an interval median; each resulting month-year is one value.
methods.censoring: Original interval endpoints are retained with a conservative closed-endpoint envelope. Monthly median bounds are medians of lower and upper endpoints. No reporting-limit substitution is used.
methods.seasonal_pairs: Compare month-year medians only with the same calendar month in another year. For each pair divide the possible difference by the integer difference in calendar years. The medians of all lower and upper pair slopes enclose the possible season-matched Sen slope.
methods.score: Each pair contributes an interval containing every feasible sign of its later-minus-earlier difference. Summed score bounds divided by the number of compared pairs give conservative seasonal ordering support. These are support bounds, not sampling confidence intervals or a significance test.
methods.coverage: The common-month calculation uses only calendar months observed in every selected year of that cohort. Daily-flow months must satisfy the explicit original-date coverage fraction; default 100 percent.
methods.sensitivity: Leave one observed year out and repeat the month-matched calculation. This identifies dependence on a particular year without deleting it from the original result.
methods.interpretation: Changes describe sampled conditions and the selected record period. Method, unit, fraction, speciation, depth and reported-versus-calculated value remain separate. Programme identifiers are retained; optionally require the same programme. No catchment load is calculated from grab samples or daily means.

sources.title: Hirsch, Slack and Smith (1982), Techniques of trend analysis for monthly water quality data
sources.use: Same-calendar-season comparison and slope; seasonality, missingness and serial correlation considerations.

sources.title: Schertz, Alexander and Ohe (1991), ESTREND
sources.use: Distinguishing censoring patterns and statistical assumptions in multi-station trend analysis.

methods.derivation: For interval x_i=[L_i,U_i], a monotone order statistic lies between the corresponding order statistics of L and U. For y_j>y_i, pair slope lies in [(L_j-U_i)/(y_j-y_i),(U_j-L_i)/(y_j-y_i)]. Taking the median of each bound preserves an enclosure. Shared observations may make individual pair extrema incompatible, so the envelope is conservative. No probabilistic claim is attached.

summary.count_basis: Source-cohort records, not a deduplicated multi-study census. Overlapping SV-833 observations in the microbial edition remain separate; datasets are never pooled.
